authoringDirection: Historical representative early-operation1963 Big Rock Point principal station exterior: partially buried spherical containment shell with equatorial rim/vertical outer ribs/crown walkway and exterior access ladder, tapered red-and-white striped stack, attached tall turbine hall with clerestory, lower two-storey front office/control block with deep vertical piers and glazing, shallow entrance canopy, and intrinsic low shoreward cooling-water building/short connecting service volume. Exclude interiors and process equipment, switchyard/powerlines, detached ancillary sheds, parking/roads/landscape/lake/shore riprap, people/vehicles/lettering and current spent-fuel storage/marker. Demolished station: historical-only, never default current-world. Use clipped spherical shell with radius19.812m/center11.2776m/top31.0896m,not a hemisphere sitting on a tall cylinder. Keep outer ribs/rim, narrow crown walkway and exterior curved ladder; no internals. Mainhall20.5m,frontblock12.5m,shorewardblock8.6m are bounded aerial-ratio estimates. Recessed front glazing/deep piers, high clerestoryband and own shallow entrance canopy. Stack73.152m with tapered shaft and seven broad alternating red/white bands; no smoke or water. Roof parapets/low vents only, no fabricated operational machinery or full-site slab. Historical viewing1963is representative, not exact photo date.
